title: Causal reconstruction: finding known graphs and equations again
summary: Synthetic time series generated from known graphs and equations (chains, forks, colliders, a feedback loop, random sparse graphs of 10 and 20 variables; noise from σ = 0.5 to 32; quadratic and source-target product terms; a delay of two rows, an effect within one row, a hidden common cause, a near-noiseless copy; and a continuous-time system sampled from every 0.1 s to every 2 s), the graph hidden, and Konjugate's causal inference asked to find it: edge precision, recall and F1, direction, and the error of the recovered equations, including where it fails.

measures.f1: directed-edge F1 (harmonic mean of precision and recall over edges with a direction)
measures.recall: share of the true edges found with their direction
measures.falseEdges: edges proposed that are not in the true graph
measures.directionAccuracy: share of the true edges found at all whose direction is reported exactly
measures.equationError: equation error: ‖estimated - true rates‖ / ‖true rates‖ over every true or proposed edge, a missing edge counting as zero
measures.foundEquationError: equation error over the true edges that were found

notes: infer fits one-row-lagged, additive models (with optional powers of a source and a source-target product) by ridge regression, after a skeleton of lag-1 partial correlations whose threshold is set from the numbers of rows and columns, the smallest significant at 5 % after a Bonferroni correction over every directed pair (docs/causalInference.md). Datasets inside that model class are recovered well; the ones outside it are included to show where it fails, and say why in their rows.

False edges in the recoverable datasets are reverse edges with small rates (the shrinkage effect docs/causalInference.md describes): each row gives the largest false edge's rate beside the smallest true rate. Less noise does not always help: the diamond with the least downstream noise (σ = 0.5) has two (x2 → x1, x3 → x1), because x2 and x3 then follow x1 closely enough to predict it, and it scores below the same diamond at σ = 2. A hidden common cause is the exception: its false edges are as strong as true ones, and nothing in the data can tell them apart.

A variable with no cause found gets no equation at all, by design (docs/causalInference.md, 'Replaying recorded values for input columns'); the own-rate error is measured only over variables with a true cause.

Rates are compared in the engine's own units, per second of the CSV's time column: an edge's terms, and a variable's own rate (its self-lag coefficient less one, over Δt). For the continuous-time datasets the true rates are the system matrix A; infer reports (Φ - I)/Δt for the sampled transition Φ = exp(A Δt), which equals A only as A Δt → 0, while at fine sampling the skeleton finds nothing: there is no sampling interval at which both the structure and the rates are right.
